<objective>
Re-skin the tablet route group — the enrolment landing page, the enable-staff-mode flow, the unlock screen
and their six components — onto the Cena design system, without moving the idle-relock timer or the PIN
behaviour.

Purpose: SC1 says Cena design tokens are "the single styling source of truth in the repo". A route group
left on the old visual layer makes that false, and it produces exactly the mixed-system outcome that
argued for re-skinning `alert`, `avatar` and `dropdown-menu` even though the imported inventory never
names them. This group is not one of SC3's eight named surfaces, and it is planned anyway rather than
quietly omitted.

Output: nine re-skinned files, all glyphs on the `Icon` wrapper, the timer and PIN behaviour untouched.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It closes the last un-re-skinned surface
group in the repo.

**This group is the one place already built to the 44px floor.** The token wave's job here is not to raise
anything — it is to not regress anything. Any control that ends this plan below 44px is a regression
introduced by the migration, not a pre-existing gap.
</objective>

  <reversibility rating="reversible">A visual pass over the three tablet pages, the PIN pad and the four action components. Both load-bearing behaviours are held rather than trusted: the idle-relock timer is asserted unchanged by a `git diff` gate that catches any timer call or multi-digit numeric literal, and the PIN pad's entry behaviour is untouched. An unattended tablet that relocks later than it used to would be a costly regression on a restaurant floor, which is exactly why it is gated rather than merely intended. Reversing is `git revert`.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Layout, spacing and type roles only.

    Apply the Cena rhythm: paper content surface, sunken page field, 24px section padding, 32px page
    margins. Page titles render at the Display role in `--font-serif`, card titles at Heading in
    `--font-serif`, body copy at Body in `--font-sans`, labels and button text at Label. Four size roles
    and two weights, never a third.

    These screens run on a tablet held in a fixed position on a counter, not in a hand, so keep the
    existing generous target sizing — do not shrink anything to match a phone layout. Every control in this
    group already meets or exceeds the 44px floor; verify none is reduced by a new spacing or height class.

    Change no string. Every user-visible string here is a Copywriting Contract row.

    Where a device code or a numeric appears, render it in `--font-mono` at the Label or Body role. The
    mono family is orthogonal to the size scale and adds no size of its own — it carries numerics and
    machine-ish strings only.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>pnpm exec vitest run tests/tablet &amp;&amp; pnpm exec vitest run &amp;&amp; pnpm exec tsc --noEmit &amp;&amp; pnpm build</automated>
  </verify>

  <action>
    Layout, spacing, type roles and glyph routing only. **Neither behaviour moves.**

    **`IdleRelock.tsx`.** Its timer duration, its reset conditions and its relock trigger are a session
    control, not a visual detail — the phase's security scope explicitly excludes session management, and
    this component is named in it. Restyle whatever it renders; change nothing about when it fires. If it
    renders no visible chrome at all, the correct diff for this file is empty, and that is a valid outcome
    to record rather than a task to force work into.

    **`NameGridPinPad.tsx`.** The name grid tiles sit on the sunken surface with ink-body names at the Body
    role. PIN keys are controls: they keep their existing generous size, which is already above the floor,
    and take the accent only as a **momentary pressed state** — one of the few places accent is permitted,
    alongside the single primary call to action, the active nav item, active chips and filters, the
    selected variant row, the "Clear filters" link and the focus ring. A PIN key at rest is not accented.

    PIN digits render in `--font-mono`. The **dot indicators are display-only and stay exempt** from the
    44px floor at their contracted 12px size with 8px gaps — they are a state display, not a target. Do not
    grow them to satisfy a floor that does not apply.

    The two PIN error rows — the wrong-PIN message and the backoff message carrying its remaining seconds —
    are Copywriting Contract rows and render unchanged. The backoff message's interpolated seconds value is
    behaviour; do not reformat it.

    Route this file's two glyphs through the `Icon` wrapper, keeping their existing size classes.
  </action>

  <action>
    Layout, spacing and glyph routing only.

    **`EnableStaffModeForm.tsx`.** Cena form rhythm: 8px between a label and its control, 16px between
    fields, 24px before the submit control. The submit control is the screen's **single primary call to
    action** and is one of the named accent-permitted places, so it takes the accent fill — and it is the
    only accented button on that screen. Azure appears once per view as the primary action; a screen with
    two accent-filled buttons is wrong. Preserve the submit-spinner and disable-on-submit behaviour exactly.

    **The three buttons.** `ExitOwnerModeButton` and `UnenrollBrowserButton` are secondary or destructive
    affordances and take no accent fill. `TabletRetryButton` is a recovery affordance on an error surface
    and likewise takes no accent. Each keeps its existing generous target size, which is already above the
    floor. Preserve each one's pending and disabled states exactly — they are behaviour, not decoration.

    **Do not change the unenrol behaviour.** That path clears cookies locally and deliberately does not
    revoke server-side, which is why it needs no authority check; a source-coverage test asserts its
    outcomes. This is a visual pass over it and nothing more.

    Route all four glyph sites through the `Icon` wrapper, keeping existing size and animation classes.
    With these four, the eighteen-site glyph migration begun in plan 01.1-07 is complete — the discipline
    test in plan 01.1-14 proves it.

    Change no string.

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale. The ASVS V3 chapter named in the register below is an out-of-scope-by-contract marker, not a review target — this plan re-skins the idle relock without reviewing its timing, which is why the gate asserts non-change rather than correctness.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| shared floor tablet → venue data | This route group runs on a device physically accessible to anyone in the restaurant. The idle relock and the PIN gate are what keep an unattended tablet from being an open session. |
| staff PIN entry → device session | The PIN pad is the authentication surface for the staff role. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-41 | Elevation of Privilege | The idle-relock timer changed under cover of a visual pass | high | mitigate | ASVS V3 is out of scope for this phase by contract and this component is named in it. A `git diff` gate asserts no timer call and no multi-digit numeric literal changed in the file. An unattended tablet that relocks later than it used to is an open session on a restaurant floor. |
| T-01.1-42 | Spoofing | PIN error copy softened or made distinguishing | high | mitigate | Both PIN error rows are Copywriting Contract rows and render unchanged, asserted by an empty `git diff` on the copy deck. The backoff message's interpolated seconds value is behaviour and is not reformatted. |
| T-01.1-43 | Tampering | The unenrol path changed during the re-skin | medium | mitigate | That path clears cookies locally and deliberately does not revoke server-side, which is why it needs no authority check. A `git diff` gate asserts no request, action or cookie call moved, and the existing outcome-coverage test is run against it. |
| T-01.1-44 | Denial of Service | A control regressed below the 44px floor by the token migration | medium | mitigate | This group was already built to the floor, so any sub-44px control at the end of this plan is a migration regression rather than a pre-existing gap. Asserted by inspecting every control-height class in the group. |
</threat_model>
